title: Bayesian posterior fusion autotrigger for SLO-drift rollbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a Bayesian posterior-fusion based automatic rollback trigger that combines multiple SLO signals (p99 latency, 95th error rate, token cost delta, throughput) into a single probabilistic decision metric. The goal is to reduce false positives from noisy single-signal thresholds while enabling fast, cohort-sensitive rollbacks during canaries, A/B tests, and shadow traffic runs. This ticket covers algorithm design, simulator to tune posterior thresholds, integration into rollout controller, and observability additions (explainable scores and traces).
acceptance_criteria: A probabilistic trigger computes P(SLOViolation | data) for each canary cohort and global traffic every minute
Trigger conditions documented: rollback when posterior > adaptive_threshold for sustained_window and hysteresis satisfied
Simulator exists that replays historical canary traces and outputs expected false positive rate (<= 2%) and mean time-to-detect degradation (<= 3 minutes) for target SLO degradations
Integration tests that run a synthetic canary (latency spike, cost spike, transient error) validate rollbacks or suppression as expected
Console exposes posterior score, contributing signals, and a human-readable rationale in rollout timeline UI
Safe defaults shipped: conservative prior, default adaptive_threshold=0.9, sustained_window=2 consecutive minutes, hysteresis=1 minute
Feature gate toggled and rollout controller respects 'bayesian_autotrigger' off-by-default for Hosted customers and opt-in for Dedicated/Private
implementation_steps: Design: formalize likelihood models per metric (latency distribution tail model, Bernoulli error model, cost relative change model, throughput drop model)
Prototype: build small Bayesian fusion microservice that ingests per-cohort metrics and returns posterior score
Simulator: create historical-replay harness that can evaluate posterior thresholds on stored canary runs
Controller integration: add posterior check hook into rollout controller pipeline with canary/A-B/shadow awareness
Alerting/OBS: add dashboard panels, traces, and per-decision debug logs; include rationale for top contributing signals
E2E tests: synthetic scenarios for latency-only, error-only, cost-only, combined correlated failures
Performance tests: ensure posterior service responds <200ms tail at 1000 queries/sec; add caching for short windows
Docs: PRD update, runbook for manual override and incident playbook
Privacy/Security: validate no sensitive payload leaves region in Private deployments (KMS/HSM audit)
rollout_plan: Start gated as experiment: enable for internal Redwood traffic on canaries only. Week 1: run in dry-run mode (compute posteriors but do not actuate). Week 2: opt-in actuation for low-risk canaries (<=1% traffic), monitor false positives. Week 3-4: expand to A/B tests and shadow traffic in Dedicated tenants. Gradually increase cohort size and lower adaptive_threshold based on simulator results. Backout path: feature gate off, immediate rollback to previous controller commit.
testing_plan: 1) Replay historical canaries with injected signals to quantify FPR and detection latency. 2) Run chaos scenarios in staging: network latency injection, model serving OOMs, token cost regressions. 3) Load test posterior service for 99.9th percentile latency. 4) Add unit tests for likelihood math and integration tests for controller hook. 5) Run human-in-loop trials where SRE/PM confirm/override first 3 actuations.
observability_requirements: Expose per-decision JSON (posterior_score, prior, likelihoods per signal, cohort_id, timestamp) to tracing and console. Dashboards: posterior_distribution over time, decision rate, false_positive_rate estimate from simulator. Add an explain panel that highlights which signals pushed the posterior up above threshold.
safety_measures: Conservative priors and high initial thresholds; sustained_window and hysteresis to reduce flapping; require at least 2 independent signals contributing 60% of likelihood mass before forced rollback unless posterior > 0.995. Manual override and emergency disable in Console. Canary-only by default for first 3 weeks.
comments: 2026-02-25 Maya Chen: Initial writeup and proposal. Chose Bayesian fusion to handle correlated noisy signals and allow principled prior incorporation.

2026-03-02 Ravi Patel: Prototype of likelihood functions ready. Latency tail uses GPD fit; error model uses Beta-Bernoulli conjugacy; cost modeled as Gaussian on relative change. Initial simulation shows promise but sensitivity to prior observed.
2026-03-05 Anya Rodriguez (PM): Wants explicit customer opt-in for Dedicated and Private, and a clear runbook for false positives. Add UX exposure for enabling/disabling per-project.
2026-03-08 SRE note - Peter Lang: Concern about posterior service scaling when many concurrent canaries run. Plan to add short-TTL memoization and shard by customer region.

2026-03-12 Ravi Patel: Implemented dry-run mode in staging. Ran three injected fault scenarios: latency spike detected at 2m30s (posterior 0.93), cost spike suppressed due to high prior; logged decisions to tracing. Next: run full simulator sweep to pick adaptive_threshold.
